findings.code: owned(path,cap) mkdir(mode=0o700) creates target/admin/noop root-owned. Child irrevocably drops to uid/gid then attempts limits(childcg), limits(target), limits(root).
findings.consequence: The code requests root-only directory traversal on target/noop then requires an unprivileged process to traverse and read below them. This deterministically fails on a normal cgroupfs honoring mkdir mode; the candidate neither verifies a different actual mode nor supplies a supported safe traversal/FD path. Do not assume cgroupfs ignores requested mode.
findings.repair: Minimal successor may set only owned cgroup directory traversal/read permissions0755 with root ownership and control files remaining root-writable only, independently check actual directory/control ownership/mode and retain exact postdrop gate. Do not grant unprivileged writes, chown cgroup controls, remove postdrop checks, or change managed-root attributes.

source_basis.observation: cgroup_create passes supplied mode to kernfs_create_dir_ns; no supported contract permits assuming mkdir0700 is ignored.
